scholarships.title: France 2030 - PEPR GFM "Grands Fonds Marins" - Appel à projets - 2026
scholarships.official_source: Agence nationale de la recherche (ANR), France 2030 / CNRS, Ifremer, IRD

eligibility: The submission file must be deposited complete on the ANR submission site before the published closing date and time, and the administrative and financial document signed and stamped by each partner institution must be deposited at the date and time indicated in the AAP.
The project scientific document must imperatively follow the template published on the call website and be deposited in unprotected PDF format.
The project must have a duration of between 36 and 54 months.
The amount of aid requested must be between 0.8 M€ and 3 M€.
The coordinating institution must be a French higher education and research institution.

The beneficiaries of the aid are research organisations and higher education and research institutions; private institutions contributing to public-service missions in higher education and research under article L.732-1 of the Code de l'Education may be financed after ANR analysis, MESRE opinion and SGPI validation.
Companies and foreign institutions may be associated as partners but cannot receive funding for that participation.
The project must fit into one or several of the five PEPR GFM challenges (Défi 1 to Défi 5).
The project must require a wide interdisciplinary and/or transdisciplinary approach as defined in section 2.2 of the AAP.
existing.eligibility_summary: Any permanent staff member can lead, but the coordinating institution must be a French higher education or research institution, the project must last 36-54 months, request 800 k€-3 M€, sit in at least one of the five PEPR GFM challenges, and be led by an eligible French laboratory.
benefits: A grant (dotation) of between 800 k€ and 3 M€ per project, disbursed by the ANR to the coordinating institution according to the schedule set in the aid contract.
Total envelope of about 17.5 M€ for this first PEPR GFM call.

Eligible expenditure is defined by the PEPR financial regulation (Règlement financier des PEPR); the AAP states the aid may for example finance equipment purchases and personnel expenditure specifically assigned to these projects, plus associated running costs.

Project running costs including the maturation phase, interaction with the PEPR GFM Scientific Council and Stakeholder and Citizen Forum, participation in PEPR GFM actions, the Data Management Plan, and travel connected with reducing the project's environmental footprint.

Personnel expenditure: the AAP expects the permanent staff involved to represent a substantial time commitment and explicitly anticipates recruiting post-doctorants, doctoral students (doctorants) and technical staff on the project.

requirements: Obtain an account (login and password) on the ANR submission site in advance; the AAP recommends registering as early as possible.
Deposit the complete submission file electronically from the project manager's account before the published closing date and time.
Only the electronic version of the submission documents present on the submission site at the call closing time is taken into account for evaluation.

Define, in the scientific document, a structured maturation phase at the start of the project, with duration, budget and responsible persons, producing an operational roadmap, an ethical issues analysis, an internal ethics charter and a Data Management Plan.
Designate a person responsible for data (référent données) who drafts and updates the PGD.
Identify, from the time of submission, a person responsible for ethical issues (référent des enjeux éthiques).
Identify among the people involved in the project one person responsible for monitoring equity and inclusion (équité et inclusion).
Describe strategies for maintaining the interdisciplinary and/or transdisciplinary dialogue throughout the project and designate the person responsible for monitoring them.

Explicitly justify in the project budget the participation of project leaders in 2 in-person meetings every 18 months in metropolitan France and 3-4 travels for workpackage leaders or staff in training (doctorate or post-doctorate) every 2 years.

Projects acquiring new data or samples at sea on unprogrammed French oceanographic fleet (IR* Flotte) means must justify why non-realisation would not undermine the project and must follow the upstream operational feasibility study procedure of the IR* Flotte (FOF naval operations pole); the minutes of the ad hoc commission (CNFH or CNFC) must be supplied.
Data management must rely on the Research e-Infrastructures tools and services (Data-Terra, Huma-num, Progedo), following FAIR and, where relevant, CARE principles.
documents: Scientific document (document scientifique): maximum 15 pages, written in English, describing the proposed project following the published template, with in appendix the list of scientific publications of the last three years by the researchers/teams proposing the project.

Administrative and financial document (document administratif et financier): covers the administrative and budget description of the project and integrates the commitment letters (lettres d'engagement) of the partner institutions.
Data Management Plan (Plan de Gestion de Données, PGD): first version within the 6 months following project start, per the ANR modalities.
Internal consortium ethics charter (charte éthique interne au consortium), written during the maturation phase.
Minutes of the ad hoc commission (CNFH or CNFC) of the IR* Flotte evaluations, where a sea campaign is integrated on not-yet-programmed fleet means.
Consortium agreement (accord de consortium), or a copy of an existing framework contract covering the same provisions, when required - see notes.
existing.english_requirement: The scientific document must be written in English (rédigé en anglais), maximum 15 pages, using the published template and deposited as an unprotected PDF.
application_method: Open an account (login and password) on the ANR submission site as early as possible.
Prepare the scientific document strictly on the published template, in English, 15 pages maximum, including the three-year publication list appendix.
Collect the commitment letters of every partner institution, signed and stamped by the legal representative, and embed them in the administrative and financial document.
Complete the administrative and financial Excel document (budget between 800 k€ and 3 M€, duration between 36 and 54 months).
Upload both documents into the dedicated 'documents de dépôt' and 'documents signés' sections of the call entry on the submission site, well before the closing time.
Validate the submission electronically before 17/11/2026 at 11:00 Paris time; an electronic acknowledgement of receipt is sent to the project manager.
Wait for evaluation by the international committee convened by the ANR.
existing.selection_notes: Only proposals satisfying the eligibility criteria (critères de recevabilité) are transmitted to the evaluation committee and can in no case be funded. Eligible projects are assessed by an independent international-dimension committee convened by the ANR, which may call on external experts and may hear project leaders (with project representatives) after sending questions in advance. The committee produces (1) a list of projects it recommends for funding on the published criteria and (2) a list it proposes not to fund because quality is insufficient on at least one criterion, with a written justification for each project, and may give an opinion on the amount requested. Uninvolved PEPR GFM programme directors then propose to the SGPI which projects could be financed and at what amount; the Prime Minister, after opinion of the CPMo and the SGPI, decides beneficiaries and amounts, and each project is covered by a contract between the ANR and the coordinating institution. Evaluation criteria fall into three groups: (a) scientific ambition and excellence (research question going beyond the documented state of the art, discipline combination justified by the question, dialogue of conceptual frameworks, ethical questions treated as integral to ambition); (b) quality of the consortium, resources mobilised and governance (recognised complementary expertise, adequacy of staff with objectives including a precise role and career benefit for each contractual worker, structured maturation phase, mechanisms for shared appropriation of questions, inventory/acquisition/management strategy for data and samples, recurrent ethical monitoring mechanisms, explicit choices to minimise the environmental footprint, coherent sizing with an argued 0.8-3 M€ budget); (c) fit with the PEPR GFM challenges and impact (clear fit with at least one challenge and the programme's strategic priorities, described scientific/economic/environmental/societal impacts, described sharing of data and results, open-access data strategy with FAIR and CARE and Opidor PGD links, dissemination to academic and non-academic audiences).
existing.best_fit: A permanent staff member (enseignant-chercheur or chercheur) at a French higher education or research institution who can lead a 36-54 month consortium and needs to build a genuinely new, wide-interdisciplinary or transdisciplinary deep-sea research consortium, typically with 800 k€-3 M€ of ANR money and with doctoral students to hire on the project budget.
existing.notes: Aid is awarded as a one-off exceptional grant, distinct from recurrent institutional funding, intended for new actions. It is a grant to an institution, not a personal scholarship: no tuition, living-cost or travel allowance is paid to individual students, and the individuals hired on a project are salaried employees of the host institution. Consortiums without companies are not obliged to conclude and transmit a consortium agreement; where required, the coordinating institution must supply it to the ANR within a maximum of 12 months from signature of the aid contract, and its absence can lead to cessation of funding and repayment under article 6.6 of the Financial Regulation. Beneficiaries must guarantee immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, deliver a first PGD within 6 months of project start, deposit data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and must mention the France 2030 support and logos in communications. Annual indicator reporting to the State and the ANR is mandatory for ex-post evaluation. Financial aid may constitute State aid under TFEU Article 107(1) and is subject to the French research State-aid framework 2022/C 414/01, the RDI exemption regime SA.111723, the de-minimis Regulation 2023/2831 and the 2011/20/EU decision.
existing.duration: Projects must run between 36 and 54 months.
existing.application_period: Ouverture : 21/07/2026 à 09:00 CEST. Clôture : 17/11/2026 à 11:00 CET. Single-phase call (l'appel à projets se déroule en une seule phase): full proposals are submitted and evaluated by an international committee set up by the ANR.
existing.deadline_display: Limite de dépôt des projets : 17/11/2026 à 11:00 CET. The application PDF cover states: "L'appel à projets est ouvert jusqu'au 17/11/2026 à 11h00 (heure de Paris)". Section "Dates importantes" repeats: all submission elements, including the documents signed by the legal representative of each partner, must be deposited electronically before 17 Novembre 2026 à 11h00 (heure de Paris).
